cards.explanation: The LORD tells Hezekiah to put his house in order, because he is going to die. Isaiah the prophet comes to Hezekiah, king of Judah, and says, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.’…” That is a heavy message, friends, and I think it lands hard. This part of the story is just heavy, so I'll let it sit.

The answer is prays. Hezekiah, king of Judah, turns his face to the wall and prays to the LORD. No speech, just a prayer. When the news is this heavy, friends, I think there's no better place to take it.

Hezekiah asks the LORD to remember how he walked before Him faithfully. He prays, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what is good in Your sight.” He's honest and plain with the LORD, with nothing fancy added. I'd want to pray the same way, friends, when I'm worn down to my last crumb.
The answer is False. As Hezekiah prays, the text says plainly, “And Hezekiah wept bitterly.” There's no staying calm here, friends, only tears. The LORD notices them too, as we'll see in a moment.

The LORD tells Isaiah to go back and tell Hezekiah His message. Isaiah hasn't even left the middle courtyard when the word of the LORD comes to him and says, “Go back and tell Hezekiah the leader of My people…” So Isaiah turns right around, like a guy halfway to the car who remembers he left his keys. The difference is that this time he's going back for the best news ever.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. I will surely heal you.” Sit with that one for a second, friends. Hezekiah went from “you will not recover.” to “I will surely heal you.” and I'd say that's quite a turn.

The place is the house of the LORD. The LORD says that on the third day from now, Hezekiah will go up to the house of the LORD. First he was told to put his house in order, and now he's getting a date to go up to the LORD's house. That's quite a turnaround, friends.

The number is fifteen. The LORD says to Hezekiah, “I will add fifteen years to your life.” Fifteen whole years added to a man who was told to put his house in order, friends. I've baked batches that didn't come out that generous.

The name is David. The LORD says He will defend the city “…for My sake and for the sake of My servant David.” Earlier in the same message, the LORD calls Himself “…the God of your father David…” The LORD says His own sake comes first, friends, and David comes right after.

The answer is a poultice of figs. Isaiah says, “Prepare a poultice of figs.” They bring it, apply it to the boil, and Hezekiah recovers. Figs are the one thing the text names, friends. I wish all my recipes were that short.

Hezekiah had asked Isaiah for a sign that the LORD would heal him. He asked, “What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?” He wanted a sign about the healing itself, friends. Isaiah then answers him with a choice.

The choice is the shadow going forward ten steps or back ten steps. Isaiah asks Hezekiah, “Would you like the shadow to go forward ten steps, or back ten steps?” It's a sign from the LORD that He will do what He has promised. Forward or back, friends, Hezekiah gets to pick.

Hezekiah wants the shadow to go back because going forward is easy but going back is not. He answers, “It is easy for the shadow to lengthen ten steps, but not for it to go back ten steps.” He picks the harder one, friends. I'd have taken the easy one and a second cookie, but Hezekiah goes for the bigger sign.

The answer is Ahaz. Isaiah the prophet calls out to the LORD, and He brings the shadow back the ten steps it had descended on the stairway of Ahaz. Ahaz was Hezekiah's father (2 Kings 16:20). The LORD does the very thing Hezekiah said was hard, friends.
